extraction.name: CONTEXTUAL
extraction.description: A novel dataset featuring human-crafted instructions that require context-sensitive reasoning for text-rich images, designed to benchmark the state-of-the-art multimodal models' capability on context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning.
extraction.creator: Rohan Wadhawan, Hritik Bansal, Kai-Wei Chang, Nanyun Peng
extraction.publisher: Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning
extraction.citeAs: Wadhawan, R., Bansal, H., Chang, K.-W., & Peng, N. (2024). CONTEXTUAL: Evaluating Context-Sensitive Text-Rich Visual Reasoning in Large Multimodal Models. Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected by sourcing images from six different sources: LAION-5B (for Time, Shopping, Navigation, Abstract), Rico Dataset (for Application Usage), Open WebText Initiative (for Web Usage), and existing VQA datasets (InfographicVQA, STVQA, ESTVQA for Infographic and Miscellaneous Natural Scenes). Images were filtered using manual or heuristic methods (e.g., PaddleOCR). Human authors then created instruction-response pairs. A verification process was conducted using MTurk workers to ensure correctness.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images sourced from LAION-5B, Rico Dataset, Open WebText Initiative, InfographicVQA, STVQA, and ESTVQA.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Images were categorized into eight visual scenarios. Heuristic-based filtering using PaddleOCR was employed for some categories to select images with high word counts. Existing question-and-answer pairs from other datasets were reannotated with novel instruction-response pairs to require context-sensitive reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images underwent manual filtering or heuristic-based filtering (using PaddleOCR to detect text and selecting top images by word count). Existing VQA datasets were reannotated with new instructions and responses. A verification process was performed by MTurk workers to filter out incorrect samples.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human authors (divided into two groups) annotated four categories each, strictly adhering to guidelines. Each sample consists of an <image, instruction, response> triplet. A verification process was conducted where MTurk workers verified the correctness of each sample. Authors also reviewed samples created by the other group to ensure adherence to guidelines and filter low-quality samples.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: 96% of the samples were found to be annotated correctly by MTurk workers. The remaining samples were reviewed by authors.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Human authors (researchers) and Amazon Mechanical Turk workers (for verification).
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset, code, and leaderboard are available on the project page. A subset of 100 samples is released as a validation set with reference responses, while the remaining 406 samples are kept hidden. The leaderboard is continuously updated.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to evaluate context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning capabilities of large multimodal models. The authors aim to ensure images and instructions are not offensive. They acknowledge that model responses may hallucinate but did not observe harmful or privacy-sensitive information. They note that human baseline performance may vary with different social groups and suggest future work on diverse regions.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The human baseline was established using annotators mainly from the US, which may introduce linguistic and writing style biases. The dataset highlights gaps in training data diversity for open models, which predominantly rely on natural scenes (e.g., COCO).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset size is 506 samples. Human evaluation is expensive and hard to scale. Open models struggle with context-sensitive reasoning compared to proprietary models. The dataset may not fully represent all social groups due to the US-centric human annotators for the baseline.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs). Specifically for evaluating context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning.
